pages.title: Neutronium Plate
pages.text: A sheet of neutron-degenerate matter rolled down to a thickness of a few femtometres, a handful of nucleons across. It is strong enough to hold back vacuum pressure and thin enough that light should barely notice it, yet it blocks everything. Bending it feels like trying to fold a mountain into a letter.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Ordinary rollers simply sank into neutronium ingots. The Casimir Vacuum Press solved it: by letting the vacuum itself push from both sides, I could squeeze the ingot evenly until it spread into a plate thinner than an atomic nucleus.
